fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance to help responders confirm the correct property from the road.
• Mark the access drive entrance clearly, as a single entry and exit point creates a bottleneck that responders need to identify quickly on arrival.
• Keep the access drive clear of parked vehicles to allow emergency apparatus to reach all three detached structures without obstruction.
• Trim dense vegetation along the access drive to maintain clear sightlines and allow larger emergency vehicles to pass without obstruction.
• Post a simple site map near the driveway entrance showing the locations of all four structures and the access drive path.
• Clear a path around the rear of the property wide enough for responders on foot to move between structures.
• Cut back dense vegetation that limits rear access so responders can reach the back of the structures without having to push through heavy growth.
• Keep any gates between the access drive and rear structures unlocked or secured with a Knox-type lock so responders can move through without delay.
• Identify a staging area on the open lawn large enough for emergency equipment and personnel that does not block the single access drive.
• Trim vegetation around all three detached structures so responders can see the walls, doors, and windows from a distance when approaching.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Thin trees within the cluster nearest to the structures to create more open space between tree canopy and rooflines.
• Remove shrubs and low brush growing directly against or within a few feet of any structure in the cluster.
• Trim low branches on large trees near the structures so branches do not hang over roofs or walls.
• Clear brush from the area with concentrated brush growth before it spreads closer to the structures.
• Thin shrubs scattered around the structures so they are separated from each other and from building walls.
• Keep the driveway clear of overhanging branches so emergency vehicles can pass through without obstruction.
• Cut back vegetation growing along both sides of the driveway to widen the clear travel path.
• Mark the single driveway entrance clearly so it is easy to identify for emergency responders arriving under poor visibility.
• Create a turnaround or pullout area near the structures if space allows, since the single access route limits how responders can position vehicles.
• Clear vegetation and debris from the rear of the structures to reduce the limited access problem at the back of the property.
• Keep the open green space free of dead plant material and avoid letting shrubs or brush spread into it from the edges.
• Remove any dead wood, dry leaves, or cut vegetation left on the ground near the structures after trimming work is done.
